summary: Added _snapshotProjectState() function to project-detail.js — extracts a flat, JSON-serializable state object from API.getProject and API.getWorkPackageOverview responses, capturing project status, last_updated, synthesis_generated, per-WP statuses and pipeline stages (flattened to { type, status, agent, rework_count }), and a health field initialised to null.

Added _diffProjectState(prev, next) function to project-detail.js — classifies snapshot pairs as 'none' (no change), 'data' (patchable in-place), or 'structural' (requires full re-render). Structural triggers: WP count change or project transition to COMPLETE/ARCHIVED. Data triggers: all other value changes including status badge, per-WP status/pipeline-stage changes, synthesis_generated, health (including null→value), and last_updated.

Created tests/gui/project-detail-snapshot.test.ts — 15 unit tests covering snapshot shape, metadata extraction, missing-field handling, WP status capture across all 5 statuses, overview enrichment, graceful edge cases, and determinism.

Created tests/gui/project-detail-diff.test.ts — 21 unit tests covering no-change detection, all structural triggers (WP count ±, COMPLETE/ARCHIVED transitions), all data-only triggers (non-terminal status, WP status/pipeline, synthesis_generated both directions, health null→value and value change, last_updated, multiple simultaneous data changes), structural dominance, and round-trip with _snapshotProjectState.
All 36 new tests pass; full suite of 3141 tests passes with zero regressions.

comments.note: _snapshotProjectState uses `s.rework_count || 0` in the pipeline stage mapping. This correctly handles the rework_count=0 case (0 || 0 = 0), but would also silently coerce null/undefined to 0 rather than preserving the raw value. Harmless given the API always emits integers, but a future hardening pass could use `s.rework_count != null ? s.rework_count : 0` for explicitness.

_diffProjectState iterates over nextIds when comparing per-WP statuses, meaning a WP present in prev but absent in next is not tracked per-field — only the wpCount mismatch captures the structural change. This is correct behaviour (count mismatch fires structural before per-WP diffing matters), but is worth documenting in the JSDoc for future maintainers.

No test currently exercises the case where a WP appears in the overview result but has a null work_package_id. The guard `if (!entry || !entry.work_package_id) return;` handles it silently. A defensive test for this would round out edge coverage, but is not required by any AC.
